identification: Edison Gem phonograph, maroon ('Red Gem') finish, Model D type (late 1908-1912, 2/4-minute; Model E also maroon, can't fully exclude), on oak base with oak domed Edison lid with handle, crank, reproducer in carriage with lift lever (looks like Model K type, unconfirmed), Blue Amberol cylinder on mandrel. Separate maroon/brown 8-panel octagonal horn with elbow, surface rust. Green painted hat-box style tin with ~35 cylinders: Edison Gold Moulded, Edison Amberol, Edison Standard Record boxes, a few red-ended boxes (possibly Edison Bell or other make) and one blue box.

viewing_check: Wind and play it: motor runs, governor steady, both speeds engage. Check the reproducer is a Model K (two styli) and diaphragm intact. Look under the white strip over the serial. Check horn seams, rust holes and elbow, lid chip, decal wear. Count cylinders, look for Blue Amberols, cracks and mould.
